source: Marcura Maritime Scope 3 Strategy Report, Section 9 (Build, Buy, Partner Strategy) and Section 10 (Implementation Priorities)
summary: License the calculation engine and factor database. Partner for vessel-level AIS precision. Build the maritime procurement, supplier engagement, and audit-trail layer. Do not attempt to build a general-purpose, independently audited calculation engine — that problem has already been solved by the market, and re-solving it would consume years without adding differentiation.

license_buy.label: LICENSE / BUY
items: Calculation methodologies aligned to GLEC Framework / ISO 14083
Factor-version management (identified in the report as inherited from the licensed engine, not built)
license_buy.note: This is a recommended strategic operating model from the strategy report, not a confirmed license or existing agreement.

partner.label: PARTNER
items: Specialist operational datasets for sea-leg precision
partner.note: The report recommends partnering, not building, this capability; no partnership currently exists.

build.label: BUILD
items: Workflow orchestration embedded in existing operational systems
build.note: The report identifies this as Marcura's differentiated, defensible layer with no direct incumbent.

implementation_priorities: Initial release: License a general-purpose calculation engine and factor database; partner with an AIS-based vessel calculation provider for sea-freight legs; build a maritime procurement taxonomy for the highest-volume Scope 3 category (vessel spares and consumables); ship a single audit-ready report type. Phase two: Extend the taxonomy to additional procurement categories; launch supplier engagement workflows with a pilot group of maritime suppliers; add IMO-aligned KPI reporting benchmarked against established shipping carbon-intensity methodologies; deepen ERP and procurement-system integrations. Phase three: Explore port-services emissions as a defined data category, in partnership with port authorities or logistics data providers given the near-total absence of existing data; pursue independent methodology certification; evaluate AI-assisted invoice classification tuned specifically to maritime procurement line items. Design constraint: Every release should ship as a feature embedded within existing maritime operational workflows, not as a new standalone platform requiring a separate login — buyers with multiple point systems already in place are unlikely to adopt an additional dashboard.
